analysis:
The PR changes only documentation in docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The one visible patch hunk is at line 2183: the `[backend] enabled_models` row now says that, when set, the list also bounds coordinator model commands and rollouts, with a link to the operator filter in configuration.md. I also read the supplied head excerpts (lines 1227-2134), which cover the stop, restart, status, doctor, models, benchmark, update, unenroll, report and logs sections. These are unchanged context, and I found no changed security-relevant content in them.

No code, controls or endpoints change, so no threat-model assumption is invalidated.

The new sentence describes a restriction on coordinator-driven model commands. That fits the trust model, in which the coordinator is trusted but the operator keeps control (TB-002, TB-003). The documentation claims enforcement, but the enforcing code is not in the supplied evidence. This is an unverified contract, not a regression. The next pass could check, if the code is in scope, that the provider rejects coordinator model commands for models outside `enabled_models` (provider-swift config and ProviderLoop handlers). No finding is raised.

The documented text makes no change to prefix-cache behavior (T-041), App Attest authorization (TB-011), or add-on hold behavior (TB-012), and no claims are altered there.
